verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents its own "full REST API for interacting with the application," with concrete endpoints for toggling flags and pulling experiment results, and its MCP server works by calling that REST API. A hands-on probe also created a user, organization, feature and SDK connection through the API. True UI parity is not shown, though: the docs say "Require confirmation" holds risky API changes until a person confirms them in the GrowthBook UI. Missing for 10: an explicit API-to-UI parity statement or endpoint coverage for metrics/fact tables, visual editor, dashboards and approval workflows; a reachable OpenAPI spec (probe found none at the checked paths); a fully headless path for confirmation-gated changes; independent corroboration of breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
the first user and organization were created through the API, a boolean feature `pa-probe-flag` was created, an SDK connection was minted
Require confirmation holds risky changes until a person confirms them in GrowthBook.
